stem: After transplanting into smaller containers with lower water-holding capacity, the previous irrigation event size produces drainage much earlier. Which adjustment is best supported?
choices: Keep the old event size because irrigation volume should remain fixed when plants are moved between containers during the same crop cycle
Increase fertilizer concentration so the smaller container retains water longer and produces drainage later in each irrigation event
Re-evaluate event size and frequency against the new container and media water-holding behavior and the crop's measured demand
Reduce monitoring for several days so the media can stabilize before deciding whether earlier drainage represents a meaningful change
rationale: Container and media changes can alter water storage and drainage. Irrigation event size and frequency should be reassessed against measured root-zone behavior rather than copied unchanged from the previous setup.
